title: Figuring the Vehicle Value Paid to a Loss Payee
content:
For the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), the vehicle value paid to a loss payee is defined by these terms.

**(a) The claim.** The claim the vehicle value is figured for is the coverage's claim with the highest claim number. Claim numbers are issued in sequence and never repeated.

**(b) The starting value.** The vehicle value starts from the actual cash value recorded on the claim's total loss declaration.

**(c) The deductible.** The deductible the vehicle value carries is the package's collision deductible, as the package schedule sets it. The deductible carried is never less than zero.

**(d) The amount.**
- The vehicle value is the starting value, less the deductible, less any total loss payment already made to the loss payee on the claim.
- It is rounded to the nearest cent at the end and is never below zero.
- A claim with neither a valuation report nor a total loss declaration has no vehicle value to pay, so the amount is zero.

### Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

Suppose a declared actual cash value of 13,275.50 USD, a collision deductible of 1,000.00 USD, and no earlier payment to the loss payee. The vehicle value is 12,275.50 USD.

With an earlier payment of 12,000.00 USD already made to the loss payee on the claim, the further vehicle value is 275.50 USD. If the earlier payment were 12,500.00 USD, the figure would be below zero, so the vehicle value is zero.
